executive_assessment.text: Selected Pespire, San Lorenzo and El Corpus communities add household coping, land access and definition-specific mobility evidence.
The Duke models report weather–violence interaction in migration associations; local water/coastal concerns are separately reported and must not be spliced into a causal violence chain.
Goascorán cooperation and WFP commitments provide capacity context, not independently verified peace gains.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2021 reports: In Pespire, San Lorenzo and El Corpus study communities, surveyed households reported drought-linked food-price and water/health burdens and livelihood interruptions; reduced food intake and savings use were common coping responses.

Source dated 2021 reports: Among surveyed agricultural workers, roughly two-thirds worked third-party land; women aged 18–29 had the highest unemployment, indicating differentiated livelihood constraints.
Source dated 2021 reports: The survey’s “forced internal migration” category explicitly includes moves for work; its results must not be equated with standard conflict/disaster displacement counts.
Source dated 2026 reports: Leaders reported irrigation-related water-access tensions around Namasigüe and Choluteca and concern in Caridad/Alianza over proposed upstream Goascorán impoundment.
Source dated 2026 reports: The analysis reports restricted traditional fishing access at Amapala beaches and mangrove-loss concerns in San Lorenzo, alongside Cedeño coastal vulnerability.
Source dated 2026 reports: The report identifies Goascorán’s binational water/adaptation cooperation as an existing capacity, while noting deforestation and intensive land-use pressures.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 17 of 18 evidence records and 2 of 2 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
No countrywide causal estimate of climate impacts on conflict or violence is established by these sources.
Full subnational coverage and independently evaluated long-term response effectiveness remain gaps.
Subnational pathway magnitudes and project-specific land-conflict conditions were not established.

Duke models use birthplace, not necessarily residence before departure, and apprehensions rather than all migration; no causal estimate of rainfall causing violence is established.
CESPAD reflects local political-economy perspectives and reported concerns; no water-flow audit or legal adjudication was inspected.
